traits.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Proteaceae: leaves usually alternate, sometimes opposite or whorled; leaves simple or compound; compound leaves usually pinnate, sometimes palmate; margins entire, crenate, serrate or dentate; veins single, pinnate, palmate or parallel; leaves evergreen; blades linear; stipules absent; leaf rosettes basal, none or terminal; plants usually hermaphrodite, sometimes monoecious, polygamous or dioecious; ovary superior; floral cup usually present, sometimes absent; stems usually woody, sometimes herbaceous; flowers in racemes, in spikes, in heads or in umbels, sometimes solitary; flowers actinomorphic or zygomorphic; perianth usually tepals, sometimes sepals and petals; fruit follicle, drupe, nut or achene; parts of each whorl 4; stamens (3-) 4; carpels 1. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py); a state the authors qualify (rarely, usually, a share) keeps its word, an unqualified one beside a usual state reads as sometimes.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Proteaceae: its irregular flowers are of no named kind (pea flower, two lips, orchid lip), read from the coded corolla symmetry (spec-rework/b1/delta): zygomorphy other. Its flowers are not mostly zygomorphic, so a plant of it states its own symmetry; one that is zygomorphic draws this kind, and one stating none is drawn regular.

traits.fruit_type.note: DELTA Proteaceae (read 2026-10-17; ~1,050 spp, ~75 genera): follicle, drupe, nutlike nucule or achene, unweighted. Wikipedia genus pages (read 2026-10-17): Grevillea (~360 spp) a thin follicle opening on one side; Banksia (~170 incl. Dryandra) woody follicles in a cone; Hakea (~150) a woody persistent fruit splitting to free two winged seeds. Some 680 follicle species, about two thirds of the family; Protea's fruit not stated on its page.

traits.leaf_division.note: DELTA Proteaceae (read 2026-10-17): simple or compound, compound leaves commonest in juveniles. Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17): Banksia (~170) single blades; Hakea (~150) mostly undivided; Grevillea (~360) simple or compound, unweighted. Simple leads among the counted ~680 species; compound confined to part of Grevillea and some rainforest genera.

traits.inflorescence.note: DELTA Proteaceae (read 2026-10-17): mostly racemes, spikes, heads or umbels, rarely solitary (Adenanthos). Wikipedia (read 2026-10-17): Grevillea (~360) paired flowers on terminal racemes; Banksia (~170) mostly spikes, Dryandra and Isostylis groups heads; Protea (83 listed) heads on a woody receptacle; Hakea (~150) loose axillary clusters (no state given, not counted). Raceme ~360 against at most ~170 each for spike and head among counted species.

traits.flower_symmetry.note: DELTA Proteaceae (read 2026-10-17): flowers regular to very irregular, unweighted. Wikipedia Grevillea (read 2026-10-17; ~360 spp, about a third of the family) zygomorphic; Hakea page (~150) gives a curved perianth tube but no symmetry word; Banksia and Protea pages silent. Only Grevillea is firmly counted, hence often over sometimes.
